text:
mike: hey support, customer reports intermittent SSE disconnects when using signed cookies. they see a clean stream for ~3-5 minutes then a 401 and connection close. can we get repro steps?

sasha: can you ask for a request_id from the failed run? also need curl copy + headers and whether they're using http/1.1 or http/2.

mike: asked and they sent back this quick curl. sending here with sensitive fields redacted:

```
curl -v -N \
  -H \"Host: api.redwood.example\" \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>\" \
  -H \"Cookie: __session=signed_cookie_here; Path=/; HttpOnly\" \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/generate?model=redwood-large
```

elena: two quick asks: 1) add `--http1.1` and `--no-buffer` (`-N`) to ensure SSE preserves chunks; 2) include `-D -` to dump headers so we can see server response headers incl `x-request-id`. example below.

```
curl -v -N --http1.1 -D - \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>\" \
  -H \"Cookie: __session=signed_cookie_here\" \
  -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \
  \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/generate?model=redwood-large\" \
  --trace-ascii curl-trace.txt
```

raj: also ask them to run with `--max-time 0` removed (so no enforced timeout) and capture around the 3-6 minute mark. we suspect signed cookie TTL vs token rotation mismatch.

mike: got a followup from customer with trace and headers, they included `x-request-id: r-0a1b2c3d`. they also said it works if they remove cookie and use direct API key, but they need signed cookies for CDN flow.

sasha: thanks. can you paste the response headers from `-D -`? need to see `www-authenticate` or any set-cookie resets.

mike: paste from trace:

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: text/event-stream
transfer-encoding: chunked
x-request-id: r-0a1b2c3d
set-cookie: __session=signed_cookie_here; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; Max-Age=300
```

and then later:

```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
content-type: application/json
x-request-id: r-0a1b2c3d
{"error":"invalid_cookie","hint":"cookie expired"}
```

elena: aha — set-cookie with Max-Age=300 looks like server resetting the cookie TTL while stream is open. streaming client won't automatically resend updated cookie for the same connection; if backend rotates cookie mid-stream we may return 401 for subsequent requests. need eng to confirm expected behavior for signed cookies vs long-lived SSE.

raj: can we reproduce locally? infra-bot: spinning up a small repro on staging with cookie TTL 180s and stream duration 10m. will post logs.

infra-bot: deployed a test job. curl command used on staging:

```
curl -v -N --http1.1 -D - \
  -H \"Cookie: __session=staging_signed_cookie\" \
  \"https://staging-api.redwood.internal/v1/streams/generate?model=redwood-small\" \
  --trace-ascii staging-trace.txt
```

infra-bot: observed same pattern: initial 200 with chunked SSE, then after ~3m server emits `Set-Cookie` and client sees `401` later when backend enforces new cookie value. logged request_ids: s-111, s-112.

sasha: for support steps to collect from customer before escalation: 1) full curl command with flags, 2) `-D -` header dump, 3) `--trace-ascii` output (or `--trace`), 4) the `x-request-id` from both 200 and 401 responses, 5) approximate wall clock times, 6) whether they route through CDN/proxy.

mike: customer uploaded trace and said they go through Fastly CDN. they shared `x-request-id` r-0a1b2c3d and timestamp.

elena: CDN could be rewriting headers or terminating keepalive. ask them to run curl directly against origin (bypass CDN) if possible to confirm. Provide example to test origin host and Host header override:

```
curl -v -N --http1.1 -D - \
  -H \"Host: api.redwood.example\" \
  --resolve api.redwood.example:443:10.0.0.5 \
  -H \"Cookie: __session=signed_cookie_here\" \
  \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/generate?model=redwood-large\"
```

raj: also recommend they try `--raw` to avoid libcurl processing chunked/transfer-encoding in odd ways. small clients sometimes conflate chunked EOF with connection close.

mike: customer ran origin bypass, same behavior. they attached both traces. 401 always references same request id on server side.

sasha: ok escalate to eng-runtime. include: customer traces, `x-request-id`, staging repro traces, and curl commands used. tag eng-runtime and paste minimal repro steps.

sasha: @eng-runtime could you check whether our signed-cookie rotation path emits set-cookie mid-stream and whether that should cause 401? include logs for request ids r-0a1b2c3d and s-111.

mike: customer confirmed they're fine with redacting tokens; sent permission to share debug bundle. attaching staging traces now.

elena: thanks — for the eng bundle include these files: curl-trace.txt, staging-trace.txt, server-side logs for given x-request-id, and network pcap if available. TODO: create debug bundle checklist and send link.

mike: will collect and attach. closing loop once eng confirms. :thumbsup:
